fixes.explanation: This one is true, friend. The LORD says, “I am not angry.” He says it right after He talks about guarding the vineyard. A guard who watches night and day and isn't angry? I think that's a surprise, and I'd have to sit down for a minute if I heard it.

The text says something different, friend. The LORD says that if thorns and briers confronted Him, “…I would march and trample them, I would burn them to the ground.” Letting them grow next to the vines isn't what He says He would do. That's the picture the verse gives.
The text pictures something much bigger, friend. It says Israel will “…bud and blossom and fill the whole world with fruit.” The fruit fills the whole world. That's a long way from one small field.

That's the reason the text gives, baker. “…for this is a people without understanding.” Then it says their Maker has no compassion on them and their Creator shows them no favor. Those are heavy words, and verse 11 puts the reason right there next to them.
